page.layout: One printed page. Top: decorative border (fleuron band), then a centred title block: heading "LECTORI BENEVOLO", subheading "S. D.". Below: a verse poem of 8 stanzas in italic with a large initial P, set in lines. Closing signature line, right-aligned, "Pantaleon Candidus / Austriacus, S. B." No margin notes. Faint show-through of the reverse page (ghost text at top) is ignored.

p.i: PErlegere ingentes cui non vacat ordine Libros, Historiæ & tumido vela dare Oceano; Sedulus exiguos legat is, relegatque libellos, Securo, tenui, vectus in amne, rate. Forsitan hæc veniet quoque per compendia eodem, Quo mora eum longa vix graue ductet iter. Pinge prius parua, quæ vis loca adire, tabella, Sic regio poterit quæque patere tibi. Corporis exiguam magni prius inspice formam, Singula quo melius membra notare queas. Qui seriem ergo cupit breuiter cognoscere Rerum Belgarum, breuis huic seruiet iste liber.

page.notes: The initial P is a large woodcut-style letter joined to "Erlegere" as printed ("PErlegere"). Line "Pinge prius parua..." and "Historiæ & tumido" are as printed. The word "vacat" and "vectus" are set in a form with an unusual long-s-like letter (printed "vacat" with a swash V, read as v); "ductet" printed with ct ligature. The first line of the verse has the word "vacat" possibly printed as "vacat"; read with [?] in doubt: "vacat"[?]. Heading "LECTORI BENEVOLO" appears in large capitals, the "S. D." in smaller capitals beneath.
